text:
Connor O'Brien: heads up: runtime train cut is tomorrow 10:00 PT. we want the build that includes the KV compaction flag plumbing (default OFF). can we confirm what PRs are in / need to be in for this train?

Benji Okafor: flag plumbing is PR 18469. default off, config keys behind `runtime.kv_cache.*`. no behavior change unless explicitly enabled. :thumbsup:

Omar El-Sayed: for the canary we also need the metrics PR (18423) in the same build, otherwise SRE is blind when we flip. allocator refactor PR 18431 is also safe (no behavior change) but it increases diff size.

Connor O'Brien: ok, so minimum set for this train = 18469 + 18423? allocator refactor can go if we’re comfortable with risk.

Kira Volkov: from LTS hardening perspective: 18431 touches some hot paths. if we can keep the train minimal, I’d prefer shipping only metrics + flag first. allocator refactor can go next train once perf-canary has a clean run.

Sean Gallagher: +1. for rollout we need (a) flag exists and is toggleable per pool (b) metrics + logs shipped so dashboards light up. we do NOT need compaction engine in this build.

Allison Grant: also please ensure metric names are stable in this build, otherwise dashboard PR in observability-pack is going to drift. do we have the final names? we’re keying alerts off these.

Omar El-Sayed: metric names in 18423 are final-ish. main ones:
- `kv_cache_fragmentation_ratio` (gauge, 0-1)
- `kv_cache_allocation_failures_total` (counter)
- `kv_cache_evictions_total` (counter)
- `kv_cache_compaction_bytes_moved_total` (counter, will be 0 until engine ships)
- `kv_cache_compaction_time_ms_total` (counter, same)
all tagged by `region`, `pool`, `model_family`.

Benji Okafor: config keys in 18469:
- `kv_cache.compaction.enabled` (bool, default false)
- `kv_cache.compaction.budget_ms_per_sec` (int, default 0)
- `kv_cache.eviction.mode` (enum, default "legacy")
- `kv_cache.compaction.trigger.fragmentation_threshold` (float, default 0.0)
NOTE: with enabled=false, the other keys are ignored.

Rafael Mendes: can we confirm the rollout sequencing expected by SRE? I want it in the release notes / oncall comms. (also: do we need a backport to the current prod runtime branch?)

Connor O'Brien: sequencing proposal:
1) ship build with metrics + flag OFF everywhere
2) validate dashboards in one hosted region (no enable)
3) later train will include compaction engine + scheduler hooks; then enable canary in 1 hosted pool + 1 dedicated pool
backport: only if we need flag in the current hotfix branch.

Sean Gallagher: re: backport: for the last incident we had no safe lever besides admission control + routing. having a no-op flag doesn’t help unless the engine is there, but metrics DO help immediately. if we can backport metrics to the current stable branch, that’s useful for next burst.

Mateo Alvarez: agree on keeping this train minimal. metrics now, compaction later. backport metrics if it’s low-risk.

Kira Volkov: if we backport 18423, please confirm it’s pure additive telemetry. no new dependencies, no high-cardinality tags beyond region/pool/model_family.

Omar El-Sayed: 18423 is additive. we were careful about cardinality (no request_id, no tenant_id). structured logs sample at INFO only on allocation failure / compaction event (compaction event won’t happen yet).

Allison Grant: can you paste the log keys? we’ll want to parse them.

Omar El-Sayed: sure, sample (from 18423):
```
{"msg":"kv_cache_alloc_failure","device":0,"pool":"hosted-usw2-a","region":"us-west-2","model_family":"llama","requested_blocks":128,"free_blocks":64,"fragmentation_ratio":0.41}
```

Connor O'Brien: ok action items:
- I’ll mark 18469 + 18423 as required for tomorrow train.
- 18431 stays out for now.
- Omar/Kira: decide if 18423 backport to `runtime-lts/2025.02` is acceptable.

Benji Okafor: one more release note: flag exists but is OFF and does nothing without future compaction engine. please don’t oversell it.

Rafael Mendes: can we also add guidance for oncall: “do not flip this flag in prod until SRE-approved canary plan” (we’ve had folks toggling random runtime configs at 3am…)

Sean Gallagher: yes please. put it in release notes + pin in #eng-oncall. we’ll treat enablement as a controlled change w/ checklist.

redwood-deploy-bot: PR 18423 marked as "Release Train: 2025.02.16" by Connor O'Brien.

redwood-deploy-bot: PR 18469 marked as "Release Train: 2025.02.16" by Connor O'Brien.

Kira Volkov: I can take the backport review. Omar, if you can open a cherry-pick PR against `runtime-lts/2025.02` today, I’ll run it through perf-canary lite + check the telemetry pipeline.

Omar El-Sayed: will do. I’ll cherry-pick 18423 only (not the allocator refactor).

Allison Grant: once merged, please ping me with the exact metric strings as they land in the release branch. I’ll update the dashboard spec to match.

Connor O'Brien: thanks all. I’ll post final train contents later today. if anything slips, we cut train without it rather than rushing.

Sean Gallagher: :thumbsup: also please make sure the config key is blocked from self-serve overrides until we’re ready (or at least scoped to internal allowlist). last thing we need is a customer toggling it via private config.

Benji Okafor: good call — 18469 wires it into the config schema but the override policy is still “internal-only” for any `kv_cache.*` keys. I’ll double-check with config service.

Connor O'Brien: perfect. closing the loop here once backport PR is up.
